criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows check_outcome_state refusing a reading for the real g6vy request 'Publish a first explainer page on how firstmate handles work.' whose criteria only say a file exists. The error names the missing observable state (reachable URL or served page). The test fails when the check is removed.
criteria.evidence: `check_outcome_state_refuses_the_g6vy_misread` (reading.rs:7524) passed when I ran it. It builds a file-only reading ('docs/explainer.md exists'). It asserts that check_outcome_state, check_reading_acceptance and refusing_check all refuse, that the error contains 'reachable URL', 'served page' and 'publish', and that refusing_check returns the name 'check_outcome_state'. The request text matches the recorded request in evidence records/jobs/2026-10/20261014-082328-g6vy/request.json word for word. Athena's fails-without-1 run, with the fix reverted, exited 101: the test does not compile without the check.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A replay test runs refusing_check over the recorded request text of all three cited jobs (20261014-082328-g6vy, 20261014-174815-7bf8, 20261017-173508-0wtc), asserts the check refuses exactly the real delivery-verb misread (g6vy) and not the other two, and asserts the caught count is 1 of 3.
criteria.evidence: `delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs` passed. I compared CITED_REQUESTS with the evidence snapshot's request.json files for all three jobs: each text is identical to the recorded one. That is better than the plan, which expected stand-in text for two of them. The test asserts caught == [g6vy], that the other two give no refusal at all, and that the CHANGELOG contains 'covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs', built from caught.len() and total. Athena's fails-without-2 run, with the fix reverted, failed with 'caught [] of 3'.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. Unit tests show acceptance when a criterion names a reachable URL or served state, for deploy, share and release as well as publish, and show no refusal for 'Add a timeout setting'. Tests show detection of 'Build the docs and publish them', 'Can you deploy the site' and 'I want to release v1'.
criteria.evidence: `check_outcome_state_accepts_a_behavior_state_for_each_delivery_verb` passed. For publish, deploy, share and release it checks three things: a reading with only a file criterion is refused; the same state text as a content criterion is refused; as a behavior criterion it is accepted. 'Add a timeout setting' is accepted. `delivery_verbs_are_found_after_lead_ins_and_markers` passed. It finds the verb in the three lead-in requests and in the list-marker forms, and finds none in 15 noun or technical uses. The corpus cases delivery-verb-after-and, -can-you and -want-to also refuse.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. Tests show an out_of_scope item such as 'Changes to shared helpers' or 'Release notes are unchanged' does not satisfy the check for a Share or Release request, and a criterion containing only 'tag' or 'URL' as incidental words (for example 'the <title> tag names the page') does not satisfy it for a publish request.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. It shows four things. (1) 'Changes to shared helpers' and 'Release notes are unchanged' are refused. (2) 'Sharing the report is out of scope', 'Releasing is out of scope' and 'Do not publish it' are accepted. (3) With two verbs, each must be put out of scope. (4) Behavior criteria such as 'the <title> tag names the page', 'The URL field is documented', 'A reader can open docs/explainer.md' and 'is available at docs/' are refused. The out_of_scope matching (out_of_scope_names) compares whole words and skips a verb followed by a NOUN_FOLLOWERS word.

criteria.criterion: Grep crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows a `step!(check_outcome_state(` line inside refusing_check, with a doc comment naming the root cause (a delivery verb read as a narrow deliverable, with no check against the state the user observes) and stating it covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs (20261014-082328-g6vy), naming the other two as outside the check.
criteria.evidence: Grep for `step!\(check_outcome_state\(` finds reading.rs:3248, inside refusing_check, right after step!(check_governance_coverage). I read the doc comment at 3649-3675. It says 'a delivery verb was read as a narrow deliverable, and reading acceptance had no check against the state the user observes' and 'This check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs'. It names 7bf8 and 0wtc as 'outside the check, which does not catch them'. The pinning test check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. The corpus has a case in which check_outcome_state refuses and a matching accepting case, and the rule that every step! has a refusing case still passes.
criteria.evidence: All 12 tests passed. They include corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome, corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms (INPUT_FORMS grew from 17 to 23), every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case, an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported and the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case. delivery_cases holds 12 cases refused by check_outcome_state, including the verbatim g6vy case, and 4 accepting cases, including delivery-verb-first-reading-names-a-served-state.

criteria.criterion: The change refuses more readings. Expected 5% of newly refused readings. A replay of past readings is expected to hold the job only above 10%. The higher refusal rate is intended: the check applies only to requests with a delivery verb whose reading names no observable state.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. replay_declaration parses the declared share as Some(5). The doc comment and the CHANGELOG both say 'refuses more readings', 'the higher refusal rate is intended' and call the figure an estimate. In Athena's own replay of accepted readings, 0 of 50 were newly refused, below the declared share plus 5 points, so the job is not held. The '1045 recorded requests' denominator matches the number of request.json files in the evidence snapshot. I did not recount the 29.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. All three pass, including the briefs.rs test that asserts READING_RULES has 6 entries.
criteria.evidence: Athena recorded all three as passing on f7766208 (CI run 42364764348). crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs is not in the diff, so READING_RULES is unchanged and its 6-entry test ran within the passing cargo test.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the root cause and the new check, with the count 1 of 3 equal to the replay test, and not claiming the other two jobs are caught. docs/decisions.md records the scope, the alternatives and the placement after check_governance_coverage. No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, toolchain or lint config) changes.
criteria.evidence: The CHANGELOG entry names the root cause and check_outcome_state, says 'the check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs, 20261014-082328-g6vy', and says the other two 'are another class ... and are not caught'. The replay test ties this count to its table. D161 records the scope (1 of 3), the alternatives (a reader rule, matching out_of_scope by substring, accepting any criterion kind, matching the verb anywhere, checking in the verifier, a glossary) and the placement after check_governance_coverage with its reason. It contains no 'supersedes' or 'amends'. Only the four deliverable files changed; no governance file did.

findings.summary: Delivery detection relies on fixed word lists, so it misses some delivery requests and falsely refuses some technical ones.
findings.evidence: delivery_verbs uses fixed lists: LEAD_INS, LEAD_IN_PAIRS, NOUN_FOLLOWERS, VISIBLE_NOUNS, DESTINATION_WORDS and AUDIENCE_WORDS. It misses 'Tag and cut release v0.5', other verbs such as ship or launch, and verbs in comma lists. It falsely refuses technical uses that have a visible-noun object, such as 'release the page lock' or 'share the report struct between crates'. D161 and the doc comment list these limits, the tests cover many technical uses, and Athena's replay found 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused, so this is acceptable for a scoped check. A later alternative is to let the reader classify the deliverable's audience as a reading field and check that field, instead of parsing the request.

findings.summary: One line of the check_outcome_state doc comment runs far past the file's usual width.
findings.evidence: Line 3650 joins two sentences ('...put the delivery out of scope. Root cause this check removes: ...') into one line of about 200 characters. rustfmt does not wrap comments, so the fmt check still passes.

summary: The candidate passes. It adds `check_outcome_state` as a step in `refusing_check`, right after the governance check. A request that uses publish, deploy, share or release as a verb with a delivery object is now refused unless the reading has a behavior criterion naming a state the user can observe, or puts the delivery out of scope by whole word. All nine criteria are met. I ran the targeted tests for each behavior criterion and all passed: the g6vy refusal, the four verbs, the lead-in forms, out_of_scope and incidental words, the declared refusal rate, and all 12 refusal_corpus tests. fmt, clippy and the full cargo test passed in Athena's recorded CI run. The replay test uses the real request text of all three cited jobs; I checked each one against the request.json in the evidence snapshot and they match exactly. The plan had expected stand-in text for two of them, so this is better than planned. The test refuses only g6vy, and the CHANGELOG and D161 claim exactly that: 1 of 3, with the other two named as another class and not caught. With the fix reverted, Athena's runs failed for criteria 1 to 3. Only the four listed files changed, and no governance file did. Two small issues remain: the detector relies on fixed word lists, which miss some delivery requests and falsely refuse some technical ones (minor; D161 lists the limits), and one doc-comment line is far too long (nit).
